introduction: These are prayers for the end of the day and for the night: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer before sleep, which commits the sleeper to God’s shelter, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s praise of prayer at midnight, when the world is quiet and others sleep. The Psalms meditate “in the night watches” and lie down “in peace”; Jesus spent whole nights in prayer; the Qur’an’s Throne Verse, said by Muslims at bedtime, speaks of the One whom “neither slumber nor sleep” overtakes. Gethsemane is the night the disciples could not stay awake.
questions: What does prayer at night have that prayer by day lacks?
The prayer before sleep hands the sleeper over to God. What is being trusted?
Is a night vigil for everyone? What do the readings say to the tired?

outside.why: If thou desirest that God open thine eye, commune with Him at midnight. He went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
In the evening I remember Thee. Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray.
Thy servant desires to sleep in the shelter of Thy mercy. I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety.
The verse Muslims recite before sleep: neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him.
When thou yearnest for meeting, at night. When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.

How sweet is prayer in the middle of nights, while others sleep. The disciples in Gethsemane: what, could ye not watch with me one hour? The readings make the vigil a delight. What do they say to those who simply fall asleep?
Prayers at dawn. Rising up a great while before day, he departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
In this hour of the night. Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night.
This servant calls upon Thee in the watches of the night. Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord. Lord, hear my voice.
